brief.label: Platform
items: LEGIC is a proprietary, closed credential ecosystem from Swiss vendor LEGIC Identsystems - cards only function within a LEGIC-licensed reader estate.
The platform is common in European corporate HQs, universities, fitness chains and leisure facilities; where those estates were built on LEGIC, replacement tokens must match it.

brief.label: Credential envelope
items: CR80 (ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1) PVC or composite cards, plus matching keyfobs - one token family across doors, lockers and time attendance.
13.56 MHz air interface with the LEGIC protocol layer; mobile extension via LEGIC Connect, the platform's smartphone credential channel.

brief.label: What to confirm before ordering

Whether your estate mixes LEGIC with MIFARE-based credentials; dual-technology cards exist but must be planned, not improvised.

author: Peter Zhang

sections.title: LEGIC cards - what they are and who needs them
sections.intro: LEGIC is not a chip you can buy on the open market and drop into any reader - it is a closed credential ecosystem from Swiss vendor LEGIC Identsystems. A LEGIC card is a token that carries a LEGIC credential, and it only works on readers licensed for that platform.
paragraphs: That closed design is the whole point - and the buying trap. European corporate campuses, universities and fitness chains built on LEGIC readers need LEGIC tokens, and those tokens cannot be swapped for a generic MIFARE card. If your facility runs LEGIC readers, you order LEGIC tokens; if you are building a new system, an open MIFARE/DESFire platform gives you more supplier choice - and we will say so plainly.

The practical test before you order: ask your facility or security manager which LEGIC platform your readers run. Token availability and encoding options depend on that answer, and we confirm it before quoting rather than after delivery.

faq.question: Are LEGIC cards the same as MIFARE cards?
faq.answer: No. Both run at 13.56 MHz, but LEGIC is its own closed ecosystem with its own protocol and reader licensing. A MIFARE card does not work on a LEGIC reader and vice versa. If your readers are LEGIC, order LEGIC tokens; dual-technology cards exist for mixed estates and we can advise case by case.

faq.question: Can you supply cards for our existing LEGIC system?
faq.answer: Yes - provided you confirm the platform generation your readers run. Send us the reader model or a photo of an existing card and we will match the token type before quoting. MOQ 500 per token type with written lead times.

faq.question: Do LEGIC cards work with smartphone mobile keys?
faq.answer: The platform's mobile extension is LEGIC Connect, which issues credentials to smartphones through the LEGIC ecosystem. Physical cards and mobile credentials are managed on the same platform; your integrator configures the mobile side.

faq.question: What is the MOQ and lead time?
faq.answer: 500 pieces per token type, consistent with our other smart cards. Every quote confirms MOQ and lead time in writing before tooling starts.
